new_external_sources.publication: C. R. Math. Acad. Sci. Paris 338 (2004), no. 8, 599–604

source_check.check_scope: The six-page published PDF was read. Theorem 3.1 states the inverse maximum principle for a nonnegative locally integrable function whose Laplacian is a measure; changing sign gives the local statement used here. The source records the theorem with attribution to Dupaigne and Ponce rather than proving it there. The book proves the required planar case directly with shrinking harmonic barriers. Its proof does not invoke an unchecked general-dimensional inverse maximum principle. Full dependencies of the paper’s general Kato theorem are not independently reverified.

internal_dependencies: Chapter 1 local bounded Bedford--Taylor measures, polar sets, plurifine locality, distributional quasi-psh representatives and almost-everywhere order
Classical harmonic Dirichlet problem on smooth planar domains, maximum principle, convolution and interior harmonic estimates
Chapter 18 Green kernel and its uniform L1 bound; atomic ideal-model classification and multiplier ideals from point Lelong numbers
Chapter 29 positive full-mass envelope characterization and one-dimensional upper-volume comparison formula
scope_boundaries: Compact connected Riemann surface and fixed smooth positive background; polar measures have mass at most the background area.
The comparison identity holds for all potentials; it is a metric on normalized ordinary models, with no positive-mass restriction.
All such models are classified by their polar curvature measures, including nonatomic polar mass and zero non-pluripolar mass.
The ideal-model subspace is closed and complete; the ideal envelope is the unique nearest ideal model and a 1-Lipschitz retraction.
Positive-mass analytic models are dense precisely in the ideal-model subspace. The analytic defect equals nonatomic polar mass.
The old complete positive-volume metric retains its distinct Cauchy condition controlling reciprocal volume.
No new capacity/L1 continuity assertion at zero mass, higher-dimensional polar-measure classification, infinite-mass extension or background-degeneration theorem is asserted.
